name: static-procs

args.prompt:
Use the attached first-eight board ONLY as our own material, lighting and contour reference. Replace the board with the NEW complete layout below; do not preserve or repeat the original eight objects. Create a clean production sprite atlas of SIXTEEN DISTINCT ORIGINAL CLOCKWORK ART RESOURCES. These are standalone static semantic sprites, NOT animation frames. The game will move, fade, rotate, or place them using its existing presentation logic.

Match the established material family: richly modeled tarnished warm brass rims and rivets, cool blue-grey steel recesses, small bright teal lenses or energy details, crisp fine pixel clusters, and controlled dark outlines. Upper-left warm light; two or three broad value planes; quiet texture. Distinct silhouettes and useful negative space, not flat vector pictograms or recolored copies.

ONE SQUARE image, requested 1024 by 1024, exactly FOUR equal columns by FOUR equal rows. Sixteen different resources, in the row-major order below. Do not crop the outer canvas. Every subject must fit inside the CENTRAL 60 percent of its own cell width and height. Leave at least 20 percent of EACH cell fully transparent along ALL FOUR sides. This leaves at least 64 percent of each cell's area transparent. No subject touches a cell edge, overlaps a neighbor, or spills a glow into the gutter. Keep every resource independently centered, including ground-based objects inside their safe region.

Use true transparent alpha for all negative space. No text, ID labels, digits, rarity borders, grid lines, background, scenery, floor shadow, painted checkerboard, opaque fog, or enormous glow. Do not repeat the same design to imply animation.

Objects:
Row 1, column 1: A teal open-eye targeting stencil with one downward needle notch and two tiny brass side lugs. A clear hollow center, not a filled target disk.
Row 1, column 2: A folded metal page glyph with a short hanging bell and one oblique engraved notch. It must read as a small magical inscription, distinct from an eye or crosshair.
Row 1, column 3: A tiny off-center bright microcore inside a split copper half-ring with one charged cyan bead. A quiet held marking glyph, not an explosion.
Row 1, column 4: A broken microcore releasing a thin three-piece brass resonance crest, a small teal crack, and a few sharp chips. Compact and brief, clearly different from its quiet charged mark.
Row 2, column 1: A thin angular teal wire-lightning segment with two offset brass beads, branching at one end. Leave most of the square transparent; no electrical storm cloud.
Row 2, column 2: A small three-tined crown-shaped electrical discharge: one main fork and two shorter forks, with copper prongs near the origin. Distinct from a wire with beads.
Row 2, column 3: Six separate low-contrast green-grey vapor wisps with tiny corroded copper flecks. Hollow, transparent center and quiet thin edges. No opaque green orb or solid fog disk.
Row 2, column 4: Two low amber ember tongues beneath a small scorched copper flake, with one quiet glowing coal. A tiny damage-tick accent, not a full enemy outline or orange cloud.
Row 3, column 1: A clipped steel shield corner with three empty clock notches and a narrow cyan lining. The center remains mostly transparent. No numbers or filled progress display.
Row 3, column 2: Two thin blue-silver protective curtain arcs attached to small hinged brass ends, with one lightly unrolling fabric edge. Elegant open middle; no opaque cage or giant bubble.
Row 3, column 3: A small stitching needle crosses one heart-shaped leaf cutout, with short brass stitches, a warm edge, and a restrained teal healing core. Transparent background and a compact silhouette.
Row 3, column 4: A small heart core caught between two closing clock hands with one bright brass catch. A compact rescue sign, not a screen-filling flash.
Row 4, column 1: A short reverse clock-hand curl with one cyan returning bead and two brass minute chips. An upward returning accent, not a long energy beam.
Row 4, column 2: ONE cracked brass bell ringing between two unequal cyan resonance brackets. A short, restrained clockwork bell accent; no heart or coins.
Row 4, column 3: ONE old brass coin with a square hole and two short curved movement streaks. A compact reward accent, without digits, price labels, or currency UI.
Row 4, column 4: A tiny opened pendulum clasp with one hanging cyan bead and one off-center clock tooth. It should read as ready to release, without text or a cost number.

SEMANTIC PRODUCTION NOTE (do not draw this text): the quiet G01 microcore is an ARMED-mark resource requiring a new real arm-transition hook; existing echo is a detonation request after deal, not that arm event. The G01 receiver stamp is reserved for positive-HP item_committed_impact/G01. The readiness clasp belongs to actual source G07 within synergy S10. The time-refund curl belongs to B06 via an explicit data source rule; the existing event omits origin. Artwork never causes HP, grants, or capabilities.

admission: Independent reviewer final_review explicitly permitted ONLY four remaining64 icon boards and selected two static16resource boards after realUI/world/frame-sequence golden. New output remains unverified.
new_animation_claim: Two static boards are 32 single-frame resources animated by original runtime age/transforms/fade, not 32 handdrawn animation sets.
